remediation_log.verdict: BLOCK (verifier-found HIGH; Q21 NO with severity 7)

findings.summary: GAP-2 receive-path bridge unreachable. marmot-ts intentionally suppresses self-echo at marmot-group.js:793 (#sentEventIds.delete → kind:'skipped', reason:'self-echo'), so the sender's own kind-445 never yields 'processed' and the applicationMessage event never fires. Even if it did, EventEmitter3's emit happens AFTER ts-mls's `yield`, making the lastIngestRumorId read off-by-one.
findings.fix: Replaced receive-path bridge with publish-path bridge (verifier's option A). Bridge mechanism: per-hTag FIFO `expectedPublishByHTag` populated by `enqueueExpectedPublish` from task-store.tsx:dispatch BEFORE sendApplicationRumor; consumed by `consumeExpectedPublishForKind445` from NdkNetworkAdapter.publish as the FIRST line. On kind-445 with matching `#h`, dequeues front and emits `publish-task` joining rumorId ↔ kind-445 eventId. Removed receive-path lastIngestRumorId map, receive-path lookup in ingestGroupEventsRaw, markPublishedRumor / clearPublishedRumorsForGroup exports.

findings.summary: FIFO correlation load-bearing on caller serialization that the bridge does not enforce. Two parallel dispatch() calls on the same group (e.g. user double-click) interleave their enqueues and would correlate rumorId↔eventId out of order.
findings.fix: Per-group dispatch publish mutex in task-store.tsx: `dispatchPublishLock: Map<groupId, Promise<void>>` using the chain-promise pattern (mirrors device-sync.ts:ingestLock). The lock brackets ONLY the `if (group)` publish block; optimistic local setState and IDB persistence run unblocked. Cross-group dispatches still proceed in parallel. Released in the inner finally and dropped from the Map when the chain becomes the tail.

findings.summary: Pre-publish failures leave stale entries that poison the next successful publish. If `createApplicationMessage`/`createGroupEvent` throws (epoch divergence, ts-mls state error), the FIFO entry stays parked and the next successful publish on the same hTag emits `publish-task` correlating the stale rumorId to a NEW kind-445 eventId. S3's classifier is automated; timestamp-skew detection is unreliable.
findings.fix: New `removeExpectedPublishByRumorId(hTag, rumorId)` export from device-sync.ts. Called inside dispatch's catch around sendApplicationRumor (BEFORE the existing console.error / CustomEvent dispatch) so the parked entry is dropped on any publish failure. O(n) splice, n≤1 in practice with the mutex from codex-1 fix.

findings.summary: marmot-ts publishes kind-445 events from FOUR sites (commits, proposals, application messages, commits-with-welcomes — all GROUP_EVENT_KIND=445 per marmot-ts/dist/core/protocol.js:43, confirmed at marmot-group.js:232/338/400/532). A commit publish from auto-invite/per-leaf-remove flows landing between our enqueue and our sendApplicationRumor's publish would dequeue OUR application-rumor entry and emit a mis-correlated `publish-task`.
findings.fix: New per-hTag in-flight counter `dispatchPublishInFlightByHTag` with `beginDispatchPublishWindow(hTag)` / `endDispatchPublishWindow(hTag)` brackets around the try/sendApplicationRumor block in dispatch. `consumeExpectedPublishForKind445` now also gates on the counter being > 0 for the hTag. Outside the window, kind-445 publishes from createCommit paths do NOT dequeue our entry. Pathological case (commit publish interleaves into our await chain WHILE counter is up) acknowledged in code comments at the `dispatchPublishInFlightByHTag` declaration; acceptable for diagnostic-only trace.

remediation_log.verdict: BLOCK (codex HIGH on residual mis-correlation under in-window commit interleave)

findings.summary: The round-1.1 window-counter scope still allows a commit publish that interleaves into our await chain WHILE our counter is up to dequeue our parked entry and emit `publish-task` with the WRONG kind-445 eventId. Codex elevated this from acceptable noise because: (a) AC-DIAG-3a makes publish-task an authoritative bridge for the F-class classifier; (b) AC-VAL-1's stability check (≤1 disagreement across 3 runs) can be deterministically wrong if the same dispatch races the same createCommit (auto-invite or per-leaf-remove from the failing-cluster tests); (c) S4 is a decision gate so a wrong F-class verdict misroutes the entire epic.
findings.fix: Replaced 'consume → immediate dequeue' with 'consume → count → defer dequeue to endDispatchPublishWindow' (verifier's option B). New module-scoped `windowKind445State: Map<hTag, {count, firstEvent}>` initialized in beginDispatchPublishWindow, populated by consumeExpectedPublishForKind445 (count++, firstEvent captured on count===1, NOT dequeued), drained in endDispatchPublishWindow. Decision logic: count===1 → emit publish-task with the firstEvent (unambiguous: mutex + awaited-publish guarantees the one event observed is ours); count>1 → emit nothing AND drop the parked FIFO entry (auto-invite commit interleaved; better to lose the trace than emit a wrong correlation; S3 classifies the test as `unknown` per AC-DIAG-3); count===0 → leave parked (defensive — cleanup-on-throw already handled the entry). 5 colocated tests in src/marmot/device-sync.test.ts cover happy path, ambiguous-2-events, no-poisoning-of-next-dispatch, out-of-window ignores, and removeExpectedPublishByRumorId regression. Test count goes from 84 to 89.

remediation_log.verdict: BLOCK (codex HIGH — verifier classified as false positive after code-trace; light remediation: lock the contract empirically with a regression test)

findings.summary: Codex claimed: when consume captures count=1 + firstEvent at the START of network.publish, and the publish then rejects (timeout / no relay ack), the dispatch's catch removes the FIFO entry but the count===1 branch still emits a stale publish-task with the failed event id. Verifier traced through the actual code at endDispatchPublishWindow:217 and showed the count===1 branch is gated on `&& front`, which is falsy when the catch has already emptied the FIFO — so no emit fires. Codex's HIGH was a misread.
findings.fix: Per the verifier's recommendation, did NOT make the structural changes codex suggested (parallel publishSucceeded bit, etc.). Instead added the regression test codex requested as the 6th colocated case in src/marmot/device-sync.test.ts: 'emits NOTHING when publish fails AFTER consume runs (post-consume throw)' — locks the contract empirically. Sequence: enqueueExpectedPublish → beginDispatchPublishWindow → consumeExpectedPublishForKind445(event) → removeExpectedPublishByRumorId (simulating the dispatch's catch on publish failure) → endDispatchPublishWindow → assert publishTaskRecords.length === 0. Test passes. The `&& front` guard at endDispatchPublishWindow:217 is now empirically locked as the publishSucceeded-equivalent. Test count goes from 89 to 90.

gap_resolutions.GAP-1: rumor.id is the canonical correlator throughout. `publish-task.taskEventId` and `task-store-accepted.taskEventId` are populated from rumor.id (no TaskEvent.id field exists). Documented inline at every site.
gap_resolutions.GAP-2: Sender-side `publish-task` emitted on the PUBLISH path (not the receive path, because marmot-ts suppresses self-echo). Mechanism (after round-1 hardening): (1) per-group dispatch mutex in task-store.tsx (`dispatchPublishLock`) serializes concurrent dispatches; (2) inside the lock, `enqueueExpectedPublish(hTag, rumor.id, groupId, rumor.id)` adds an entry to a per-hTag FIFO `expectedPublishByHTag`; (3) `beginDispatchPublishWindow(hTag)` increments a per-hTag in-flight counter `dispatchPublishInFlightByHTag`; (4) `await sendApplicationRumor(rumor)` fires marmot-ts's chain ending at `network.publish(applicationEvent)`; (5) `consumeExpectedPublishForKind445(event)` is the FIRST line of NdkNetworkAdapter.publish — gated on (event.kind===445) AND (#h tag matches a pending entry) AND (dispatchPublishInFlightByHTag>0). When all gates pass, dequeues the FIFO front and emits `publish-task`; (6) on throw, dispatch's catch calls `removeExpectedPublishByRumorId(hTag, rumor.id)` to drop the parked entry; (7) `endDispatchPublishWindow(hTag)` runs in the finally regardless of success/failure. The window-counter scoping discriminates application-rumor publishes from concurrent commit/proposal publishes on the same kind-445/#h (marmot-ts has FOUR kind-445 publish sites — all GROUP_EVENT_KIND=445 per marmot-ts/dist/core/protocol.js:43). Pathological case: commit publish interleaves into our await chain while the counter is up — still mis-correlates, acknowledged in code comments. Cleanup: `clearExpectedPublishesForHTag(hTag)` (clears both the FIFO and the counter) is called from `refreshGroupSync` on group teardown using the still-held entry.group reference.

notes: S2 inlines mlsTrace.record(...) calls at every site enumerated in spec.md § Stories S2 and § Trace event shape, plus the GAP-2 publish-path bridge for sender-side `publish-task` correlation hardened across three remediation rounds. All recording is gated on the S1 module's build-time check (`process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_TRACE_MLS === "1"`); when unset, every record() resolves to the no-op default with empty body and the install block in client.tsx is dead-coded out. `make test` 12 files / 90 tests (was 84 baseline — +6 from new colocated bridge tests in device-sync.test.ts) and `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0. Two existing applicationMessage listeners (device-sync's persistence and task-store's React state) are NOT collapsed; they receive different trace hooks per AC-HOOK-10's split semantics.
